method:
Chain scored street segments into corridor windows, normalize, weight, rank.

Input : out/segments_scored.parquet (segments.py)
Output: out/corridors_ranked.csv      every window, raw means + normalized dims + 3 totals + ranks
        out/corridors_top25.json      top 25 non-overlapping windows under each weight set,
                                      raw values behind each score
        out/e138_position.json        where the East 138th design corridor lands under each set

Chaining. Segments with the same normalized street name inside one borough form a
graph on shared endpoints (snapped to 1 ft). For each connected component the trunk
is the longest shortest-path (graph diameter, weighted by length). Windows slide
along the trunk: from each trunk segment, extend until the window is >= TARGET_KM
(1.6 km, the East 138th design length) or the trunk ends; windows shorter than
MIN_KM (0.8) are dropped, none exceed MAX_KM (2.0). A window's members are every
segment of that street (both carriageways of a divided street too) whose midpoint
projects into the window's chainage and lies within 60 m of the trunk.

Window value = length-weighted mean of member segments. Each dimension is then
normalized citywide as a percentile rank across all windows (0..1, ties averaged),
oriented so that 1 = strongest case for a green corridor. Rank-based, not min-max,
because exposure, income and asthma are heavy-tailed and min-max would let a few
outliers flatten the rest. The Du Bois dimension is a length share, already 0..1.

Dimensions
  exposure    rank(exposure)                          higher = closer to bridge / ramp / highway
  monitor     rank(monitor_signal) among windows that have a monitor within 1.5 km; null otherwise
  health      mean(rank(adult asthma ED), rank(child 5-17 asthma ED))
  econ        mean(rank(-median income), rank(poverty rate), rank(NFH rank number))
  heat        rank(HVI)
  hw          0.5 * share of length with H/W < 0.5 + 0.5 * rank(-H/W)
  canopy_gap  rank(-trees per 100 m)
  dubois      share of length within 400 m of a below-grade or elevated highway

Weights (each sums to 1)
  equal        every dimension 1/8
  burden       exposure .15 monitor .10 health .15 econ .15 heat .15 | hw .12 canopy .12 dubois .06
  feasibility  hw .20 canopy .20 exposure .20 | monitor .08 health .08 econ .08 heat .08 dubois .08

Missing dimensions are not imputed. The total is the weighted mean over the
dimensions a window actually has, with the weights renormalized, and
dims_missing lists what was absent.
normalization: percentile rank across all windows (ties averaged), oriented so 1 = strongest case; dubois is a length share
